newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal to authorise foreign investments -paper.
newsitem.headline: Portugal to authorise foreign investments -paper.

text.p: Portugal's economy ministry plans to sign authorisations for foreign investments by German group Siemens AG, U.S. carmakers Ford Motor Co and General Motors Corp and S.Korea's Halla Engineering and Construction Co, a Lisbon paper reported.
The Diario de Noticias quoted a source in the ministry as saying the investments totalling 50 billion escudos ($294 million) would create some 3,000 jobs in Portugal.
Economy ministry spokesmen were not immediately available.

The paper said the main investment planned was a 10 billion escudos joint venture by Siemens and Japanese group Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd to build microchip circuits in Evora in southeastern Portugal.
It said Ford was planning to expand its output of electronic components in a two billion escudos investment at its installations near Setubal, south of Lisbon.
Ford was also planning to invest in a joint venture with Halla to manufacture air conditioning compressors, it added.
The paper said General Motors was planning to boost its investment in Portugal, but it gave no details.
The Diario de Noticias said the ministry was studying other applications for foreign investments in Portugal totalling 200 billion escudos which it hoped to approve later this year.
